help.introEn: An essay in economic history of about 750 words on the year 1923, told through prices: a loaf of bread that cost 250 marks in January cost 200 billion in November; a dollar stood at 4.2 trillion marks on 15 November; wages were paid twice a day and carried home in laundry baskets. The text explains how it came to this, who lost and who gained, how the Rentenmark brought the end and why Germans still think differently about money from their neighbours a hundred years later. Numbers of this size demand a language that compares and places them, and that is exactly what you practised last: advanced comparison. Einer der größten Vertrauensbrüche der Geschichte; bei weitem der höchste Preis; um das Tausendfache teurer als; je länger die Krise dauerte, umso schneller; nicht annähernd so viel wie; zehnmal so viel wie, doppelt so hoch wie. Then there are the compounds that make up economic language and that must be taken apart to be understood: Papiermark, Rentenmark, Reparationszahlungen, Notenpresse, Sachwertbesitzer, Vertrauensverlust.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: In November a loaf cost a billion times more than in January, and by no means only in Berlin.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The longer the crisis lasted, the faster the notes lost their value, until a day counted as much as a year before.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: A multiple takes so … wie: zehnmal so hoch wie. Als belongs to the comparative (höher als), not to so.
help.tips[0].en.title: Comparing in large numbers
help.tips[0].en.text: einer der größten + genitive plural (one of the biggest breaches of trust) · bei weitem / mit Abstand der höchste (by far the highest) · um das Tausendfache / um ein Vielfaches teurer als (a thousand times more expensive than) · zehnmal so viel wie, doppelt so hoch wie (so … wie with multiples, not als) · nicht annähernd / längst nicht so viel wie (nowhere near as much as) · je länger …, umso / desto schneller · immer schneller (increase without a comparison point). Wrong but common: doppelt höher als; correct: doppelt so hoch wie or um das Doppelte höher als.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Whoever owned real assets, houses, machines, shares, survived the devaluation; whoever had monetary wealth lost everything.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The printing press ran day and night; thirty paper mills and 130 printing works worked for the Reichsbank.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: The last element (Zahlungen) is the core; the first (Reparationen) says what for: payments for reparations, i.e. war compensation.
help.tips[1].en.title: Taking economic compounds apart
help.tips[1].en.text: The last element determines kind and article; the earlier ones describe: die Papiermark (paper mark, unbacked), die Rentenmark (mark backed by Renten = land charges), die Notenpresse (press for banknotes), die Reparationszahlungen (payments for reparations), der Sachwertbesitzer (someone who owns real assets), der Vertrauensverlust (loss of trust), die Geldentwertung (devaluation of money). Linking -s after -ung, -heit, -tion, -tät: Zahlungsmittel, Inflationsrate.
help.rememberEn[0]: Multiple with wie (zehnmal so hoch wie), comparative with als (um das Zehnfache höher als).
help.rememberEn[1]: Compound: last element = core and article; Papiermark, Rentenmark, Notenpresse, Sachwert.
help.examEn: Essays in economic history with figures, causes and long-term consequences are a typical reading text in the C2 exam.
help.hookEn: 250 marks in January, 200 billion in November, for the same loaf. Read how a country lost its money in a single year and why it still talks about it today.
